channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: Can we trust LLMs to judge whether a research idea is novel?
item.description: Ai2's Old Ideas, Novel Problems tests six LLM novelty judges on 154 high-novelty ICLR 2026 ideas and finds prompt wording shifts accuracy by over 50 percentage points, with a specialized system trailing a simple Claude Opus 4.6 baseline. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation
item.description: Genie 4 delivers real-time interactive world simulation with native audio—music, ambient sound and dialogue—while Gemini Omni anchors visual realism and other Gemini models maintain coherence, opening now as a research preview to Project Genie trusted testers. (Google DeepMind)

item.title: OpenAI expands partnership with Oracle to bring its apps to ChatGPT
item.description: OpenAI and Oracle are expanding their partnership to bring Oracle business applications and AI agents into ChatGPT and power new Oracle offerings, with Oracle citing 130,000 ChatGPT users and 95,000 Codex users. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Build specialized multimodal models with LFM3
item.description: Liquid AI's LFM3 puts text, vision and audio models on one shared backbone in the 2B parameter range, enabling single-GPU fine-tuning, with LFM3-1.7B about 25% faster than LFM2-1.2B at 8K context. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Codex CLI 0.165.0
item.description: Codex CLI 0.165.0 ships alongside GPT-6.1 Terra in ChatGPT Work and Codex on Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu plans, a fast model for reasoning about images and screens, then acting precisely in browsers and on desktops. (OpenAI Codex Changelog)

item.title: GitHub Copilot assisted permissions generally available
item.description: Assisted permissions are generally available in GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot app and Visual Studio Code, where a large language model evaluates command, file-path and URL requests, auto-approving clearly safe ones while requiring user approval for the rest. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: [AINews] Anthropic files for $2T IPO in 2 weeks: 1400% growth rate, 48% of revenue through cloud partners, 85% margin, $1B op profit in Q2, $134B cash in bank and $10B lifetime burn
item.description: Anthropic's public S-1 shows revenue rising from $41M in 2023 to $16.3B in H1 2026, Q2 revenue of $11.6B up 1,368% year over year, and $974M in Q2 operating profit, as Latent Space analyzes the Nasdaq-bound filing.

item.title: Greptile takes bug detection beyond code review with GPT-6 Astra
item.description: Greptile uses GPT-6 Astra’s computer use to resize a browser to iPhone dimensions and simulate users finding hidden buttons, while Codex cuts code rollbacks and Daybreak strengthens security. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
item.description: Anthropic plans an IPO with a public benefit corporation, a five-trustee long-term benefit trust appointing four of seven directors via Class T shares, and a Founder LLC holding 50.1% voting power, as experts question whether safety-first governance survives market pressure.

item.title: 🔮 Anthropic’s S-1 in charts
item.description: Azeem Azhar's 39-chart breakdown of Anthropic's S-1 shows more than 80% of current revenue comes from models launched within six months, while growth is slowing and Q3 may post a marginal loss due to foundation payments.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO Prospectus: 11 Details to Note — a Hundred-Billion-Dollar Raise, an $80.7 Billion Loss, and a $7 Controlling Stake
item.description: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals a $100 billion raise, an $80.7 billion loss and a $7 controlling stake, and this breakdown of 11 details examines the financial and governance logic behind the offering's most contested points.

item.title: OpenAI asks outside experts, including a Nobel laureate, to check proofs its AI produced in math, computer science, and physics
item.description: OpenAI has enlisted outside “shepherds,” including a Nobel laureate, to verify AI-generated Lean proofs in computer science, math and physics, among them a claimed refutation of the ETH for SAT that could undercut hundreds of papers.

item.title: OpenAI says its AI model has achieved three scientific breakthroughs, spanning the local smoothing conjecture, the exponential time hypothesis, and Yang–Mills theory
item.description: OpenAI said on October 27 its AI model proved the all-dimension local smoothing conjecture, refuted the exponential time hypothesis, and supplied a four-dimensional QCD and pure Yang–Mills existence proof, with the first two Lean-verified and physics awaiting review.

item.title: Dissecting Anthropic's Prospectus: 11 Details Behind Its Plan to Raise About $100 Billion in IPO
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO prospectus, ticker ANT, targets $100 billion at a $1.5 trillion-$2 trillion valuation, with revenue up 30-fold in five quarters and Q2 operating profit of $974 million, as an 11-detail breakdown also flags an $80.7 billion first-half net loss.

item.title: How We Built Our Design Agent
item.description: LangChain's Slack-based design agent Content Studio turns a single prompt into coded assets such as videos, slides and social images, producing over 3,000 assets and 80-plus slide decks while cutting per-request model cost from about $8 to roughly 50 cents.

item.title: With Google SynthID detection in Gemini, anyone can easily check if an image, video, or audio file was made with AI from Google.
item.description: Users can now ask Gemini "Is this AI generated?" to check whether an image, video or audio file was produced with Google AI, as SynthID detection rolls into Gemini to help people judge content authenticity online.

item.title: How Check Point accelerates vulnerability research with Daybreak
item.description: Check Point cuts vulnerability research from hours to minutes with OpenAI Daybreak and turns vulnerability intelligence into customer defenses, protecting more than 100,000 organizations. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Gamma5 reshapes thinking and design, with deep integration across 20+ mainstream office tools
item.description: Gamma5 reshapes thinking and design, with deep integration across 20+ mainstream office tools (AIbase)

item.title: Anyone can now bring their ideas into the company codebase
item.description: Replit's Cloud Agents let non-engineering staff such as design and customer service submit tested pull requests to the company's core codebase in natural language, with engineers still controlling releases, now available to all Pro and Enterprise customers.

item.title: Databricks & the Future of the Firm
item.description: Databricks hit a $7 billion revenue run rate, up 80% year over year at a $190 billion valuation, and a16z's Ben Horowitz explains how agent queries outnumbering human ones plus 17 million-plus daily database launches reshape Lakehouse and Lakebase.
